title: Build and run a container
intro: Your Mini Bank API code is in this folder, along with a `Dockerfile` (the recipe). Let's build the container and run it.
welcome: Practice terminal ready. Type help at any time.

always.output:
FROM python:3.12-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install -r requirements.txt
COPY . .
CMD ["uvicorn", "main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"]

steps.explain: Docker is there. On your own computer you'd install **Docker Desktop** first.

steps.goal: Build an image from the Dockerfile and name (tag) it `mini-bank`.
steps.hint: `docker build -t mini-bank .`. The full stop at the end means *use this folder*.
steps.output:
[+] Building 18.2s (10/10) FINISHED
 => [1/5] FROM python:3.12-slim
 => [2/5] WORKDIR /app
 => [3/5] COPY requirements.txt .
 => [4/5] RUN pip install -r requirements.txt
 => [5/5] COPY . .
 => naming to docker.io/library/mini-bank:latest
steps.explain: Docker followed the recipe step by step and produced an **image**: a sealed kit with Python, your libraries and your code inside.

mistakes.output: ERROR: "docker buildx build" requires exactly 1 argument.
mistakes.say: You're missing the `.` at the end: it tells Docker which folder to build from.

mistakes.output: (builds, but the image has no name)
mistakes.say: That builds an image with no friendly name. Add `-t mini-bank` so you can refer to it.
That works in real life! For this exercise please use the name `mini-bank`.

steps.goal: List your images to check it's there.
steps.output:
REPOSITORY   TAG       IMAGE ID       CREATED          SIZE
mini-bank    latest    5c2f1a9e8b7d   10 seconds ago   162MB
steps.explain: Your image is ready to run anywhere Docker runs: your laptop, a colleague's, or a cloud server.

steps.goal: Run it, connecting port 8000 on your computer to port 8000 in the container.
steps.output:
INFO:     Started server process [1]
INFO:     Application startup complete.
INFO:     Uvicorn running on http://0.0.0.0:8000 (Press CTRL+C to quit)
steps.explain: A **container** is a running copy of the image. `-p 8000:8000` is like a phone extension: calls to 8000 on your laptop are put through to 8000 inside the container. You could now open http://localhost:8000.

mistakes.say: It's running, but sealed off: without `-p 8000:8000` nothing outside the container can reach it. Add the port mapping.
The port needs two numbers: `outside:inside`, so `8000:8000`.

steps.goal: In a second terminal, list the running containers.
steps.output:
CONTAINER ID   IMAGE       COMMAND                  STATUS         PORTS
9b1c0e2d4f5a   mini-bank   "uvicorn main:app --…"   Up 12 seconds  0.0.0.0:8000->8000/tcp
steps.explain: There it is, up and running. `docker stop 9b1c0e2d4f5a` would stop it.
